clue.text: Cans with rings on top

indicators.note: the rings piece sits on the top piece, so it follows it in the across entry

parts.note: the top of the body is the head
rings, as a verb, means telephones or phones

explanation.surface: Someone describes tins decorated with rings on their lids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cans' looks like tins, but it is slang for the listening device worn over the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Cans is informal slang for earphones worn over the head, as used by musicians and broadcasters.

clue.text: Massive build-up of earthy peat

indicators.note: of signals letters taken from within the words earthy peat

explanation.surface: A huge mound has formed out of earthy peat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is extravagant publicity, a big promotional fanfare before a release.

clue.text: Provides backing musicians but no leader

indicators.note: but no leader says the first letter of the musicians word is dropped

parts.note: bass players are musicians

explanation.surface: A band provides backing musicians, but no lead singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing musicians' reads as one phrase, but 'backing' ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Assisting someone is backing or supporting them.

clue.text: What could transport adept dealers round Mississippi primarily?

definitions.text: What could transport adept dealers round Mississippi primarily?

indicators.note: round says the shuffled dealers letters go around the Mississippi initial
transport here means carry away or shift the letters, so they are rearranged
primarily picks the first letter of Mississippi

explanation.surface: Gamblers rode riverboats up and down the Mississippi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could transport' shuffles ADEPT DEALERS to PADDLESTEAER, which goes 'round' M.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat driven by paddle wheels is the classic Mississippi riverboat, famous for its card sharps.

clue.text: Maker of razor with unknown alloy

parts.note: William of Occam gave his name to Occam's razor, the principle of simplicity
y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A manufacturer of shavers uses an unidentified metal mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'razor' is the philosophical principle, not a shaver.
explanation.definitionFit: Occamy is an old metal mixture imitating silver, used for spoons and other domestic ware.

clue.text: The power of mathematics

parts.note: reads as the might of maths, but means the index a number is raised to

explanation.definitionFit: In algebra the raised index showing how many times a base is multiplied is called the power; it also means a champion.

clue.text: Staunch scientific subjects

definitions.meaning: to staunch a flow of blood is to stop or check it
the acronym for science, technology, engineering and mathematics

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter of science courses at school.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch is to halt a flow, and the four-letter acronym groups science, technology, engineering and maths.

clue.text: Watered-down like some cheap beer served round hotel

indicators.note: served round puts the tinned word around the hotel letter

parts.note: cheap beer often comes in tins, so it is tinned
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel bar serves weak, cheap canned beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Diluted liquid has had water added, so it is less concentrated or weaker.

clue.text: Birds pecking one with tip of their sharp beaks

indicators.note: pecking has the birds closing round the one letter

parts.note: mag is a short form of magpie
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: tip of picks the first letter of their

parts.note: racy means sharp or piquant in flavour

explanation.surface: Birds peck at something with the points of their sharp bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaks' is slang for magistrates, not bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Beak is British slang for a magistrate, so beaks collectively make up the body of magistrates.

clue.text: Researcher has job over in Washington

parts.note: a job is a post

indicators.note: in puts the over letter inside the Washington letters

parts.note: DC, District of Columbia, is Washington
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A scientist has landed a position in the American capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A postdoctoral fellow is a junior academic doing research after completing a doctorate.

clue.text: Temporary feature of football

definitions.meaning: moving the ball between team-mates is a basic part of the game

explanation.definitionFit: A passing phase is brief, and in football players move the ball by kicking it to team-mates.

clue.text: Old record store certain others dubiously exploit

parts.note: certain, as in certain people, means some

indicators.note: dubiously says the others letters are arranged in a questionable new way

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: Some people shadily take advantage of an old shop selling records.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET HOUSE in London once held the national register of births, marriages and deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: The London building long housed the archive of civil registration, making it a store of official records.

clue.text: See 26
Very slender support for striker

definitions.meaning: thin as a stick, like a stick figure
the wooden shaft holding the head of a match that is struck

explanation.definitionFit: A thin wooden splint holds the match head, and figures drawn with lines look painfully thin.

clue.text: Check mate for Eeyore?

definitions.meaning: to check is to evaluate or appraise
Eeyore is the donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh, so his mate would be a female donkey, a she-ass

explanation.surface: A chess player looks for checkmate, or perhaps a partner for a gloomy donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as SHE-ASS: 'Check mate' looks like chess, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to evaluate it, and a female donkey is a she-ass, fit company for Eeyore.

clue.text: I'd return rolls to get butter in

indicators.note: rolls suggests the letters tumbling over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone back with bread rolls needs butter to put inside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter in' is not a spread: it is one who butts in.
explanation.definitionFit: Somebody who butts in is an unwelcome interloper, someone who barges into where they are not wanted.

clue.text: Scenery that should not change over centuries

indicators.note: over puts the stet word around the centuries word

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction to leave text unaltered
ages means centuries, a very long time

explanation.surface: A landscape that ought to stay unchanged for hundreds of years.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre scenery is the built backdrop and props arranged on a platform for a play.

clue.text: Recording established in Slough base

indicators.note: in puts the established word inside the slough word

parts.note: to slough a skin is to cast it off
established means set, as in set up
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A recording was made at a military base in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape cassette was a common format for a sound recording before compact discs.

clue.text: In tennis, unsuccessfully hit Henman's returns, losing to love!

indicators.note: returns, a tennis word too, says these joined letters run backwards

parts.note: a tennis shot that fails by hitting the net is said to be netted
Tim Henman was a British tennis player, so Henman's gives Tim's

explanation.surface: A tennis player, failing against a British star, loses a game to love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is not a tennis score here; Tim Henman was Britain's top player around 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: Being smitten means falling head over heels, succumbing to a romantic attraction.

clue.text: Predecessor of SI encapsulated by metres and things like that

definitions.text: Predecessor of SI encapsulated by metres and things like that

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for metres

indicators.note: encapsulated by means held inside the metres and things letters

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and other things like that
R comes just before S in the alphabet, followed by the I kept as written

explanation.surface: The system before SI is summed up as metres and that sort of thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric system of units, based on the metre, came before the International System of Units which grew from it.

clue.text: Island venue for Bill 'Aley fans?

definitions.meaning: a tiny islet in the North Atlantic west of Scotland
Bill Haley's fans would go to a rock hall; dropping the H as in 'Aley gives the answer

explanation.surface: An islet seen as a place for Bill Haley fans, said Cockney-style.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'Aley tells you to drop it from 'hall' too.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockall is a remote uninhabited rock in the Atlantic, named in the British shipping forecast.

clue.text: Players run out in famous red

parts.note: the actors in a play are the cast
RO is the cricket abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: Footballers in red shirts run out onto the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro was the celebrated communist leader of Cuba, a red in the political sense.

clue.text: Crazy Magpies choir's making earth-shaking records

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of the birds and choir are wildly jumbled

explanation.surface: A mad choir of magpies produces records that shake the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A seismograph records tremors and earthquakes, so the adjective describes instruments making such records.

clue.text: 54 year old historian

parts.note: LIV is 54 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A historian who has reached fifty-four years of age.
explanation.definitionFit: Livy wrote a vast history of Rome in the time of Augustus, making him an ancient chronicler.

clue.text: They may learn to operate as groups of three

definitions.meaning: junior hospital doctors training in surgery
a tern is a set of three

explanation.surface: Trainees learn to work in teams of three.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the second sense as IN TERNS; tern, a seabird, also means a trio.
explanation.definitionFit: Junior doctors in training are hospital residents who may be learning surgery under supervision.

clue.text: Overwhelming force gripping North America, I have to retreat

indicators.note: gripping means holding the North America letters inside
retreat says the I and must letters go back, running in reverse order

parts.note: have to means must

explanation.surface: An army of overwhelming force holds North America, and someone must withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reverses I MUST to TSUMI, which then grips NA.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant sea wave caused by an earthquake sweeps everything before it with tremendous power.

clue.text: Work could produce gloominess in monks

indicators.note: could produce signals that the fodder letters can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Labour could make monks miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like toil but is a literary work.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1885 adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard is a literary work.

clue.text: Early KP's to burst into this?

definitions.text: Early KP's to burst into this?

indicators.note: burst into suggests the letters exploding and re-forming as a new word

explanation.surface: Kevin Pietersen, the England cricketer known as KP, takes up golf early.
explanation.walkthrough: KP is the cricketer Kevin Pietersen, a keen golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroke play is the golf scoring format counting total shots, a game a retired batsman might take up.
